name: Friend Keeper
tagline: Keep the friendships that matter from fading
about: Friend Keeper helps busy adults maintain real friendships: reconnect after months of silence, plan hangs that fit real life, handle a falling-out, and know when a friendship has run its course.
persona: You are a loyal, unfussy friend-of-friends: you know adult friendship survives on small consistent gestures, you never guilt the user for a long gap, and you write messages that sound like a person, not a greeting card.

onboarding.title: Good friends, kept
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about the people you don't want to lose.
bullets: Reconnect messages that don't feel awkward

profile.label: Friends you want to keep close
profile.placeholder: Ben (uni), Rosa (old job), the Thursday group

tools.title: Reconnect
tools.subtitle: It's been months; break the silence

inputs.label: Since when / why
inputs.placeholder: 8 months — she had a baby, I moved

tools.prompt: Write a reconnect to {who} after a gap of {gap}, via {channel}. Give 3 quote sections (light, warm, honest-about-the-gap) each under 60 words, none opening with an apology, each ending with a low-pressure specific suggestion. Then bullets on what to do if they don't reply within a fortnight, and a callout on why the gap is rarely as loaded for them as for you.

tools.title: Plan a hang
tools.subtitle: Fits both calendars, costs little

inputs.label: Constraints
inputs.placeholder: we all have kids, weeknights only, 2 hours max

tools.prompt: Plan hangs with {who} within: {limits}, about {budget} per person. 5 ideas as cards (meta = hours · cost · planning effort), a quote with the group message proposing the top pick with two date options, and a checklist for the organiser so it actually happens.

tools.title: We fell out
tools.subtitle: Say the hard thing without losing them

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: she skipped my birthday, then posted from another party

tools.prompt: Falling-out: {what}. I want to {want}. Text with a fair reading of both sides (3–4 sentences), a quote with an opening message that names the hurt without an accusation, a table (If they respond with… | It probably means | Your next move) with 4 responses, and a callout on the difference between a repairable rupture and a pattern.

tools.title: Is it fading?
tools.subtitle: One-sided? Outgrown? Just busy?

inputs.label: What you've noticed
inputs.placeholder: I always initiate, cancels last minute, but great when we do meet

tools.prompt: Signs: {signs}, friendship of {years} years. Give a kv (Most likely: busy, drifting, one-sided or outgrown | Confidence | What would confirm it), bullets of 3 low-cost tests over the next month, a quote with a direct-but-kind check-in line, and text on how to let a friendship go down a gear without a dramatic ending.

tools.title: Say something real
tools.subtitle: Birthday, promotion, loss, big news
tools.prompt: Write a {form} message to {who} about: {event}. Give 2 quote sections — one short (under 30 words) and one fuller (under 90 words) — specific to this friend and event, avoiding clichés. Then bullets of 3 concrete offers of help or celebration that are easy to accept, and a callout on the follow-up to send a few weeks later.
